lines.text: Here's a server that does ten milliseconds of work per request, on average.
lines.caption: Here's a server that does ten milliseconds of work per request, on average.

lines.text: Send it eighty requests a second, and it's working eighty percent of the time: it's eighty percent busy.
lines.caption: Send it eighty requests a second, and it's working eighty percent of the time: it's eighty percent busy.

lines.text: A request then takes fifty milliseconds on average, from arrival to reply.
lines.caption: A request then takes fifty milliseconds on average, from arrival to reply.

lines.text: Send it ninety requests a second, an eighth more traffic, and it's ninety percent busy.
lines.caption: Send it ninety requests a second, an eighth more traffic, and it's ninety percent busy.

lines.text: Requests now take a hundred milliseconds.
lines.caption: Requests now take a hundred milliseconds.

lines.text: You might expect a little more traffic to mean a little more delay.
lines.caption: You might expect a little more traffic to mean a little more delay.

lines.text: Instead, the response time doubled.
lines.caption: Instead, the response time doubled.

lines.text: Why?
lines.caption: Why?

lines.text: And even at eighty percent, where do forty of those fifty milliseconds come from, when the work only takes ten?
lines.caption: And even at eighty percent, where do forty of those fifty milliseconds come from, when the work only takes ten?

lines.text: A request's response time has two parts: the time the server spends working on it, and the time it spends waiting for the server to be free.
lines.caption: A request's response time has two parts: the time the server spends working on it, and the time it spends waiting for the server to be free.

lines.text: The work takes ten milliseconds on average, however busy the server is.
lines.caption: The work takes ten milliseconds on average, however busy the server is.

lines.text: So at eighty percent busy, a request waits forty milliseconds in a queue, four times the average work.
lines.caption: So at eighty percent busy, a request waits forty milliseconds in a queue, four times the average work.

lines.text: At ninety percent, it waits ninety.
lines.caption: At ninety percent, it waits ninety.

lines.text: The question is really about queues.
lines.caption: The question is really about queues.

lines.text: Why do they get so long, when the server still has time to spare?
lines.caption: Why do they get so long, when the server still has time to spare?

lines.text: Suppose requests arrived evenly spaced, and every one took exactly ten milliseconds.
lines.caption: Suppose requests arrived evenly spaced, and every one took exactly ten milliseconds.

lines.text: At ninety percent busy, ten milliseconds of work fills ninety percent of the gap between requests, so a new one arrives about every eleven milliseconds.
lines.caption: At ninety percent busy, ten milliseconds of work fills ninety percent of the gap between requests, so a new one arrives about every eleven milliseconds.

lines.text: It finds the server already done with the last one.
lines.caption: It finds the server already done with the last one.

lines.text: Nobody ever waits, and every response takes ten milliseconds, even at ninety percent busy.
lines.caption: Nobody ever waits, and every response takes ten milliseconds, even at ninety percent busy.

lines.text: Real traffic varies in two ways.
lines.caption: Real traffic varies in two ways.

lines.text: Requests arrive at random, so sometimes several come close together.
lines.caption: Requests arrive at random, so sometimes several come close together.

lines.text: And some requests need much more work than others.
lines.caption: And some requests need much more work than others.

lines.text: When a clump arrives, the server can only work on one at a time, and the rest wait in a queue.
lines.caption: When a clump arrives, the server can only work on one at a time, and the rest wait in a queue.

lines.text: So queues come from variability.
lines.caption: So queues come from variability.

lines.text: What decides how long they last?
lines.caption: What decides how long they last?

lines.text: A queue shrinks only when the server finishes work faster than new work arrives.
lines.caption: A queue shrinks only when the server finishes work faster than new work arrives.

lines.text: At eighty percent busy, new work keeps arriving at eighty percent of what the server can do.
lines.caption: At eighty percent busy, new work keeps arriving at eighty percent of what the server can do.

lines.text: So while there's a queue, only the other twenty percent of its effort actually shrinks it.
lines.caption: So while there's a queue, only the other twenty percent of its effort actually shrinks it.

lines.text: Call that twenty percent the spare capacity: it's what clears the queue.
lines.caption: Call that twenty percent the spare capacity: it's what clears the queue.

lines.text: At ninety percent busy, the spare capacity is only ten percent.
lines.caption: At ninety percent busy, the spare capacity is only ten percent.

lines.text: On average, the same queue takes about twice as long to clear, and more requests pile on while that happens.
lines.caption: On average, the same queue takes about twice as long to clear, and more requests pile on while that happens.

lines.text: That's the intuition; the exact answer comes next.
lines.caption: That's the intuition; the exact answer comes next.

lines.text: Here's the same random stream of requests at both loads.
lines.caption: Here's the same random stream of requests at both loads.

lines.text: At ninety percent, the queue builds higher and lasts longer.
lines.caption: At ninety percent, the queue builds higher and lasts longer.

lines.text: The fraction of time a server is busy is called its utilization.
lines.caption: The fraction of time a server is busy is called its utilization.

lines.text: For the simplest case, queueing theory gives the exact average response time.
lines.caption: For the simplest case, queueing theory gives the exact average response time.

lines.text: The case is one server, requests arriving at random, each unrelated to the others, and work times that vary just as randomly: mostly short, sometimes several times longer.
lines.caption: The case is one server, requests arriving at random, each unrelated to the others, and work times that vary just as randomly: mostly short, sometimes several times longer.

lines.text: The answer is the work time divided by the spare capacity: ten milliseconds divided by one minus the utilization.
lines.caption: The answer is the work time divided by the spare capacity: ten milliseconds divided by one minus the utilization.

lines.text: At fifty percent busy, that's twenty milliseconds.
lines.caption: At fifty percent busy, that's twenty milliseconds.

lines.text: At eighty, fifty.
lines.caption: At eighty, fifty.

lines.text: At ninety, a hundred.
lines.caption: At ninety, a hundred.

lines.text: At ninety-five, two hundred.
lines.caption: At ninety-five, two hundred.

lines.text: A simulation of twenty million requests at each load lands on the curve.
lines.caption: A simulation of twenty million requests at each load lands on the curve.

lines.text: It's almost flat at first, then steep.
lines.caption: It's almost flat at first, then steep.

lines.text: From eighty to ninety percent, the spare capacity halves, and the response time doubles.
lines.caption: From eighty to ninety percent, the spare capacity halves, and the response time doubles.

lines.text: From ninety to ninety-five, it halves and doubles again.
lines.caption: From ninety to ninety-five, it halves and doubles again.

lines.text: So that's where the forty milliseconds went: not into work, but into waiting.
lines.caption: So that's where the forty milliseconds went: not into work, but into waiting.

lines.text: A little more traffic halved the spare capacity, from twenty percent to ten, and the response time doubled with it, from fifty milliseconds to a hundred.
lines.caption: A little more traffic halved the spare capacity, from twenty percent to ten, and the response time doubled with it, from fifty milliseconds to a hundred.

lines.text: Burstier traffic, or more variable work, makes this worse.
lines.caption: Burstier traffic, or more variable work, makes this worse.

lines.text: Bigger clumps of requests, or a few very long ones, build bigger queues, and the same spare capacity takes longer to clear them.
lines.caption: Bigger clumps of requests, or a few very long ones, build bigger queues, and the same spare capacity takes longer to clear them.

lines.text: So they need more spare capacity for the same response time.
lines.caption: So they need more spare capacity for the same response time.

lines.text: That's why capacity plans leave headroom.
lines.caption: That's why capacity plans leave headroom.

lines.text: Decide how slow requests may get, and read a first estimate of the load limit off the curve.
lines.caption: Decide how slow requests may get, and read a first estimate of the load limit off the curve.

lines.text: On this curve, if a request may take five times its work time on average, keep the server at or below eighty percent busy.
lines.caption: On this curve, if a request may take five times its work time on average, keep the server at or below eighty percent busy.

lines.text: Real systems, with burstier traffic and more than one busy resource, usually need more headroom than this curve says.
lines.caption: Real systems, with burstier traffic and more than one busy resource, usually need more headroom than this curve says.

lines.text: These are averages, and some requests take several times longer.
lines.caption: These are averages, and some requests take several times longer.

lines.text: The slowest requests are the next lesson.
lines.caption: The slowest requests are the next lesson.

lines.text: And never plan to run a server at a hundred percent busy.
lines.caption: And never plan to run a server at a hundred percent busy.

lines.text: With no spare capacity, nothing clears the queue, and it keeps growing.
